title: Flooring Software: 5 Tools for Quotes, Jobs and Reviews
html:
Flooring software starts with a quote app, a review tool and a free map listing. Jobber lists $49 a month with no commitment, Joist Pro lists $17 a month and NiceJob lists $95 a month. Add a free Google Business Profile and a fast website so homeowners can find you. Published prices below run from free to $135 a month for the main plans.

Flooring software has to do three jobs: price the room, schedule the install and collect reviews that win the next quote. Most flooring companies buy a scheduling app and ignore the other two. This guide sorts five tools by the job each one does, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Flooring is a measure-and-quote trade. A homeowner often gets three estimates, and trust decides the winner when prices are close. So this list covers the quote, then the reviews and calls that build trust.

Which flooring software handles quotes, jobs and invoices?

Jobber and Joist are the two tools a flooring company should compare first. Jobber runs the whole job. Joist focuses on the estimate and the invoice.

  • Jobber: online booking, scheduling, quotes, invoices with online payments and a simple website. The Core plan for one user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually. Limit: extra users cost $29 a month each, and card payments cost 2.9% plus 30 cents.
  • Joist: estimates, invoices and online payments in a light app. Joist Pro is $17 a month billed monthly, with unlimited documents. Limit: the lower Basics plan caps you at 5 documents a month, and Joist lists a processing fee on payments taken through it.

A flooring quote needs square footage, a waste allowance, the material, the underlayment and removal of the old floor. Build one template per floor type so every quote lists the same line items. A homeowner comparing three quotes reads a clear line-item quote as a sign of a careful installer.

Pick Jobber when two or more crews need a shared calendar. Pick Joist when one owner quotes and installs and only needs paperwork.

Which tool tracks the calls that book flooring jobs?

CallRail is a call tracking tool that gives each marketing source its own number, so you can see which one produced a booked estimate. It does not write quotes or schedule crews.

  • CallRail: its Lead Tracking plan is $50 a month and includes 5 local numbers, 250 local minutes and 25 texts. Plans bill monthly or yearly, with a 14-day free trial. Limit: usage above the included amounts is billed extra, and each added local number costs $3.

Flooring companies often get calls from a showroom sign, a Google listing, a paid ad and a builder referral. Without separate numbers, they all look the same. Two numbers, one on the website and one on the Google listing, already show whether search or your own site books more estimates.

Which free tool puts a flooring company on the map?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows your flooring company in Google Maps and local search. Google states you can add or claim your business at no charge.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, hours, photos and reviews when a homeowner searches for flooring installers nearby. Limit: it only stands out if you keep photos and review replies current, and Google's paid ad products are separate.

Before and after photos suit this listing well. Upload new ones after every finished room.

How much does flooring software cost a year?

A lean flooring stack costs $204 a year. A fuller stack with reviews and call tracking costs $2,088 to $2,328 a year at published prices.

ToolPublished priceYearly cost
Jobber Core, no commitment$49 a month$588
Jobber Core, billed annually$29 a month$348
Joist Pro, billed monthly$17 a month$204
NiceJob Starter$95 a month$1,140
NiceJob Pro$135 a month$1,620
CallRail Lead Tracking$50 a month$600
Google Business ProfileFree$0

Yearly cost is the published price multiplied out. Prices read from each vendor in November 2026.

Here is the arithmetic. The lean stack is Joist Pro at $17 a month plus a free listing, which is $204 a year. A fuller stack is Jobber Core billed annually at $348, NiceJob Starter at $1,140 and CallRail at $600, which is $2,088. Swap Jobber to the no-commitment price and it is $49 plus $95 plus $50, or $194 a month, which is $2,328.

Divide the yearly cost by your job count to see the real price. As an example, $2,328 a year across 120 installs is $19.40 per install. That is small next to the margin on one floor, so judge each tool by the jobs it saves, not the plan price.

Watch the costs that sit outside the plan price. Card processing, extra users and add-ons such as Jobber's Marketing Suite at $99 a month can double a small plan. Ask each vendor for a full monthly total before you commit.

What should you test in flooring software before you buy?

Test the parts of the job that flooring makes hard. A demo built for a plumber hides them. Run these six checks inside each free trial.

  • Square footage: can a quote line be priced per square foot and still show the room total?
  • Waste allowance: can you add a waste percentage as its own line, so the homeowner sees why the order is larger than the room?
  • Deposits: can the invoice take a deposit before the material order, and the balance after the install?
  • Multi-day jobs: can one job span several visits, such as demolition, prep and install?
  • Photos: can the crew attach before and after photos to the job from a phone?
  • Quote follow-up: does it remind you to chase an open quote after a few days?

A tool that fails two of these checks will cost you time every week. Drop it, even if the price is lower. The cheapest plan is the one that your crew stops using in the first month.

How do you ask flooring customers for a review?

Ask on the day the crew finishes, by text, with a direct link to your Google review page. A short request sent at the right time beats a long email sent a week later.

  • Step 1: walk the finished floor with the homeowner and ask if they are happy with it.
  • Step 2: send the review link by text within the hour, before the day moves on.
  • Step 3: send one reminder a few days later to anyone who has not replied.
  • Step 4: reply to every review, good or bad, within two days.

Tools such as NiceJob automate steps 2 and 3. They do not replace step 1. The walk-through is where the homeowner decides how they feel, so keep it in your own hands.

What does flooring software not do?

Flooring software does not bring in new homeowners. It organizes work you already have. A company with an empty calendar needs lead sources before it needs a better scheduler.

It also does not fix a slow quote. If estimates go out three days after the visit, a new app only makes the delay easier to see. Set a same-day rule first. Then let the software enforce it.

How do you choose flooring software?

Choose flooring software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: can it list square footage, waste and underlayment as separate lines, and send the quote by text or email the same day?

Cost: add the plan price, extra users and card processing fees, then compare the total against one average install.

Setup effort: can one person load price lists and customers in a weekend, or does it need training?

If you are...Start withAdd nextSkip for now
A one-person installerGoogle Business Profile and Joist ProReview requests after each jobCall tracking and crew scheduling
A shop with two crewsJobber Core or ConnectNiceJob StarterReview automation beyond requests
A showroom with paid adsJobber plus CallRailNiceJob Pro for referralsAnything that duplicates your scheduler

A decision table built from the prices in this guide. Match your size to the row, then confirm each price with the vendor.

Test each trial with one real job. Quote a recent room from your own notes, send it to a friend as a test, and time how long it takes. The tool you finish fastest in is the one your crew will actually use in the busy season.

Software does not create demand, so pair it with lead sources. Search ads from flooring Google Ads reach homeowners ready to book an estimate. Rankings from flooring SEO bring steady local calls.

The website matters as much as the tools. A flooring site wins estimates with a page per floor type, a gallery of finished rooms and a quote form. That is a managed build, not a do-it-yourself builder.

What software does a flooring company need?

A flooring company needs a way to quote rooms, schedule installs and take payment. Jobber and Joist cover those jobs. It also needs a free Google Business Profile and a review tool so homeowners can find and trust you before they pick between three quotes.

How much does flooring software cost?

Published plans in this guide run from free for Google Business Profile to $135 a month for NiceJob Pro. Jobber Core lists $49 a month with no commitment, and Joist Pro lists $17 a month billed monthly. Extra users, payment fees and call tracking cost more.

Is Jobber or Joist better for a flooring company?

Jobber runs scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, so it suits a shop with several crews. Joist handles estimates and invoices, so it suits a one-person installer. Jobber Core lists $49 a month with no commitment, and Joist Pro lists $17 a month billed monthly.

Do flooring companies need review software?

Review software helps when you finish jobs faster than you ask for reviews. NiceJob lists Starter at $95 a month for review requests by text and email. You can start free by sending your Google review link by hand, then add a tool once volume grows.

Is Google Business Profile free for a flooring company?

Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: photos of finished floors, accurate service areas and a reply to every review. Google's paid ad products are separate from the free listing.

Does a flooring company need a website if it uses job software?

Yes. Job software runs the work after a homeowner picks you, but it does not bring homeowners in. A website with a page for each floor type, a gallery and a quote form gives them a reason to ask you for an estimate.

What should a new flooring company buy first?

Set up a free Google Business Profile and a quote app such as Joist Pro first. Then add a simple website with a quote form. Add review software and call tracking once you run ads or finish enough jobs to make follow-up hard to do by hand.

Review software helps when you finish jobs faster than you ask for reviews. NiceJob lists Starter at $95 a month for review requests by text and email. You can start free by sending your Google review link by hand, then add a tool once volume grows.
###
Is Google Business Profile free for a flooring company?
Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: photos of finished floors, accurate service areas and a reply to every review. Google's paid ad products are separate from the free listing.
###
Does a flooring company need a website if it uses job software?
Yes. Job software runs the work after a homeowner picks you, but it does not bring homeowners in. A website with a page for each floor type, a gallery and a quote form gives them a reason to ask you for an estimate.
###
What should a new flooring company buy first?
Set up a free Google Business Profile and a quote app such as Joist Pro first. Then add a simple website with a quote form. Add review software and call tracking once you run ads or finish enough jobs to make follow-up hard to do by hand.
